alkylation concentration: Afterwards, proteins were alkylated using 10 mM IAA for 30 min at ambient temperature (approximately 22 °C) in the dark.
cleavage agent: For all samples, trypsin in 100 mM TEAB in water was added to the S-Trap.
enrichment method: the SEC-enriched pool corresponding to the void peak was treated using Top 14 protein depletion columns
fractionation method: Filtered ascites or plasma-derived serum samples were loaded onto a 1.5 × 12 cm Sepharose CL-4B gravity flow column
fragmentation method: within those 3 s the most abundant ions/scan were selected for fragmentation by higher energy collision dissociation (HCD).
instrument: All peptide digests were analyzed using reversed-phase (RP) liquid chromatography on an UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano system coupled to an Orbitrap Eclipse Mass Spectrometer.
ionization type: Peptides were eluted directly from the tip of the column and nano sprayed into the mass spectrometer.
labeling: The Orbitrap Eclipse was operated in data-dependent mode.
mass analyzer: MS spectra were collected in the ion trap in rapid scan mode (centroid mode).
ptm: Oxidation of methionine residues (+15.995 Da) variable; deamidation of asparagine, glutamine, and arginine (+0.984 Da) variable; Carbamidomethylation of cysteine residues (+57.021 Da) static; N-terminal glutamate to pyroglutamate (−17.027 Da) on peptide terminus variable; protein N-terminal acetylation (+42.011 Da) variable

Oxidation of methionine residues (+15.995 Da) and deamidation of asparagine, glutamine, and arginine (+0.984 Da) were set as variable modifications. Carbamidomethylation of cysteine residues (+57.021 Da) were set as a static modification. In addition, N-terminal glutamate to pyroglutamate (−17.027 Da) on peptide terminus and protein N-terminal acetylation (+42.011 Da) were set as variable modifications.
reduction reagent: Briefly, proteins were denatured and reduced simultaneously using 0.4% DCA, 10% SDS, and 10 mM TCEP with incubation at 95 °C for 10 min.
